products.name: Loom AI
products.note: Async video AI; auto-chapters; summaries; transcription; Atlassian acquisition context

reading.body:
Loom AI applies video understanding to async work by automatically generating chapters, summaries, and transcription from screen recordings, reducing friction in knowledge transfer for distributed teams.

Video is a high-bandwidth way to communicate technical context, but it scales poorly without indexing and search. Loom addresses this by extracting structured metadata from recorded sessions, making video content retrievable by topic and searchable by transcript. The integration with Jira shows how this approach extends into developer workflows, where automatic capture of device, browser, and error data transforms ad-hoc recordings into actionable bug reports.

This product sits upstream of compute demand, not downstream of it. Loom does not generate video or require the power-intensive inference that image generation or large language models demand. Instead it processes and organizes video that already exists, which means it reduces friction in communication without directly driving the infrastructure scaling that constrains AI. The data does not cover Loom's own compute footprint, inference costs, or how the Atlassian acquisition factors into enterprise adoption and usage volume.

profile_text.body:
Loom is a screen recording and video sharing service, per its own site. It describes itself as a free screen recorder for Mac and PC, an online screen recording tool with advanced video editing and video storage, and says it is trusted by over 22 million people, with sharing from Loom.com.

On the AI side, the site describes a workflow where a recorded walkthrough is turned by Loom's AI into a fully populated Jira work item in a few clicks. Loom automatically captures technical details for developers, including device, browser, and OS information, console errors, and network activity, to help pinpoint problems. The product tracked for the company is Loom AI, described as async video AI with auto-chapters, summaries, and transcription, alongside Atlassian acquisition context. No litigation, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for Loom.
